items.t: Said she was honored to be a co-author of a bill to create a task force concerning Native women and girls.
items.q: “This task force is a crucial step in ensuring that Native women and girls are seen, heard, valued, and believed,” said Rep. Peggy Flanagan (DFL – St. Louis Park). “I’m honored and humbled to be a co-author of this bill.”

items.t: Said voters should choose a Senator who will work to end the illegal war in Iran, among other priorities (2026).

items.t: Held a signing ceremony with Governor Tim Walz for Executive Order 23-03, protecting the rights of Minnesota's LGBTQIA2S+ community to seek and receive gender-affirming health care.
items.q: On Wednesday March 8, Governor Tim Walz and Lieutenant Governor Peggy Flanagan held a signing ceremony for Executive Order 23-03, protecting the rights of Minnesota’s LGBTQIA2S+ community to seek and receive gender-affirming health care.

record.t: Has served as Lieutenant Governor of Minnesota since 2019.
record.q: Peggy Flanagan has served as the Lieutenant Governor of Minnesota since 2019.

record.t: Was one of two DFLers to chief author a bill that became law during the 2017-18 session.

record.t: Was elected to the Minnesota state legislature in 2015.

record.t: Won Minnesota's U.S. Senate race, defeating Republican Michele Tafoya.
record.q: Democrat Peggy Flanagan won Minnesota's US Senate race Tuesday, defeating Republican Michele Tafoya in a closely watched midterm contest for the seat held by retiring Sen. Tina Smith.
